question.problem: A lottery decides that $3$ out of every $20$ lottery tickets will win a special prize. If a player wants to win a special prize, what is the probability of finding a prize before purchasing their $5$th ticket? Round your answer to $3$ decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
A geometric random variable $X$ with probability of success $p$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=(1-p)^{x-1}p
$$

Let $X$ be the number of tickets purchased until a special prize is found. On average, the chance of finding a special prize on a single ticket is 

$$
p=\frac{3}{20}=0.15.
$$

So, the number of tickets that the player should purchase before they find a special prize can be modeled as a geometric random variable with a probability of success $p=0.15.$

So, $X∼\text{Geom}(0.15).$ In this case, $X$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =(1-0.15)^{x-1}(0.15) \\  & =(0.85)^{x-1}(0.15)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the probability of finding a special prize before the $5$th ticket is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<5) & =P(X\in \{1,2,3,4\}) \\  & =f(1)+f(2)+f(3)+f(4) \\  & =(0.85)^{1-1}(0.15)+(0.85)^{2-1}(0.15)+(0.85)^{3-1}(0.15)+(0.85)^{4-1}(0.15) \\  & =(0.15)+(0.85)(0.15)+(0.85)^{2}(0.15)+(0.85)^{3}(0.15) \\  & =[1+0.85+(0.85)^{2}+(0.85)^{3}](0.15) \\  & ≈0.478\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.
